EXPLANATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULELENG REGENCY NUMBER 5 OF 2019
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL EXPLANATION.
The purpose of the establishment of the State is stated in the fourth paragraph of the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia which states that "The State protects all Indonesian people and all Indonesian territory and to promote general welfare, educate the life of the nation and participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice". The meaning of protecting here includes protecting every citizen including from all forms of violence. In addition, Article 28 G paragraph 2 of the 1945 Constitution states that every person has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity. Thus the right to obtain protection from acts of violence is guaranteed by the constitution.
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights. Women and children victims of violence must have their dignity and honor protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Buleleng Regency, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of Regional Regulations.
Protection of women and children victims of violence in the Regency requires institutional and regulatory support that can guarantee its implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection efforts for victims specifically in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Buleleng Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Buleleng Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Buleleng Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Buleleng.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Buleleng Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
8. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband and wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and his/her child, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
9. Every person is an individual or corporation.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
11. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
12. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred.
15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human worth and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
16. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
17. Cooperation is an activity or effort carried out by several people to achieve common goals.
18. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
19. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
20. Victim recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence, both physically and psychologically.
21. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and Legal Aid.
22. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as Repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

2.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, there is no provision about training/capacity building for implementers/institutions (e.g., police, P2TP2A staff, service providers) as an institutional mechanism. The cited bases are misinterpreted: (i) Pasal 23 only says the Regional Government conducts “pembinaan dan pengawasan” (guidance/supervision) of P2TP2A and other social institutions—this is oversight, not a mandate to train or build capacity. (ii) Pasal 22 lists SPM performance indicators referring to “petugas terlatih/tenaga kesehatan terlatih” (trained officers/health workers), but it does not establish a training program, capacity-building plan, or obligations to conduct training; it is merely an indicator/benchmark. (iii) Pasal 8 mentions seminars/workshops and counseling as prevention activities aimed outward (socialization/education to prevent violence), not capacity building of institutions. Therefore the judge over-read these provisions as capacity building, producing a false positive; the golden ‘No’ aligns with the Indonesian text.

3.2.evaluator_rationale: The text mentions the need for “special service rooms within the police force,” but it does not establish or describe a specialised police service unit for VAW within police offices (i.e., a dedicated unit/structure), only facilities supporting integrated services.

3.2.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly requires police-based specialized facilities: Pasal 11 ayat (2) huruf a states services must be supported by “ruang pelayanan khusus di jajaran kepolisian” (special service rooms within the police). This is a concrete specialized police service facility/unit element (at least a dedicated ‘special service room’ structure) for handling cases, which matches the indicator’s intent of specialized police service provision. The judge’s ‘No’ was based on an overly narrow interpretation that only a formally named ‘unit’ counts; however the regulation does establish/require a specialized service room in the police. Since this relevant information was present in the retrieved candidates (Article 11(2)(a)), the golden label ‘Yes’ appears correct and the discrepancy is best explained by the evaluation being too strict rather than missing evidence.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly includes a special protection category for children with disabilities, indicating disability-targeted special protection measures (though framed for children rather than women with disabilities).

Article 5
Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.
Letter b What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Letter c What is meant by "economic violence" is an action that restricts a person from working inside or outside the home to produce money and goods, including allowing a person who works to be exploited, while someone does not fulfill the economic needs of the family.
Letter d What is meant by "social violence" is an act of a person or group of people that causes injury or loss of life of a person or can cause physical damage or damage to another person's property.
Letter e What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
Letter f What is meant by "Domestic Neglect" is:
a. actions that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;
b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should be;
c. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person;
d. actions that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.
